title: Design: WorkerSession — separate execution truth from card views (provider trait, principals, reaper, headless testing)
raw_text:
Design: WorkerSession — separate execution truth from card views (provider trait, principals, reaper, headless testing)

## STATUS (as of 2026-06-14)

**Program: PR0–PR11 (several slices split into sub-PRs). PR0–PR6 are MERGED; PR7 (token→session authority flip) is the keystone, next.** PR6 shipped as **4 sub-PRs**. This issue stays open through PR11. For the live status snapshot + in-force decisions + corrections to the original design, see the **pinned CURRENT STATE comment**; this body is the design-of-record.

| PR | link | shipped |
|---|---|---|
| PR0 | #683 | Characterization anchor — frozen gate-denial vectors (**51**, write-entry black-box) + CI freeze gate; event-serde goldens; FSM edge-table golden; exit-arbitration matrix golden; prod-snapshot migration-replay harness; CASCADE pin; dead-worker-stall L2 pin |
| PR1 | #689 | `calm-types` + `calm-exec` (traits only); ids/Event-data/model/WaveLifecycle moved; Principal/WorkerContract/SessionMode/Liveness/WorkerSession added; ActorId frozen; `pub use` shims; ts-rs removed from calm-server |
| PR2 | #697 | `calm-truth` crate (entrance + sqlite + 44 migrations moved wholesale); `worker_sessions` DDL (0045, incl. `requester_session_id`); `DecisionGate` trait (`&mut WriteTx`) + `PermissiveGate`; scoped T1–T4 conformance |
| PR3a | #703 | Raw-`UPDATE runtimes` absorption (harness side): 4 matrix-bypassing raw status writes → named eventless calm-truth `*_tx` entrances; harness status framed as a **T2 phase-mirror watermark** |
| PR3b-i | #705 | `runtimes`↔`worker_sessions` **dual-write in one tx** keyed `session.id == runtime.id`; `derive_session_identity(kind)` (never `card.role`); boot backfill; Layer-1/Layer-2 parity |
| PR3b-ii | #706 | Layer-3 boot-time full parity diff, env-gated `NEIGE_ASSERT_WORKER_SESSIONS_PARITY_ON_BOOT` (default OFF) — the PR9b-retirement precondition |
| PR4 | #707 | Raw event-append absorption (saga side): 9 `event_append_for_operation_tx` callers → gated `append_decision_event_in_tx<G>` (`&PermissiveGate`); parallel entrance **deleted**; T4 firewall + CI gate |
| PR5 | #708 | `FakeProvider` + `FakeRoot` + in-memory full-loop e2e (zero processes); `GatedDecisionSink` (test-only defender); defends FakeRoot through PR6/PR7 rewrites |
| PR6a-1 | #710 | `calm-provider` crate (DAG-firewalled, no calm-server dep) + 3 real `WorkerProvider` impls (terminal/claude/codex) + `CodexDaemonProbe` + L3 conformance; additive, no caller rewire |
| PR6a-2 | #713 | Reaction seam — **`CardDecisionSink`** (Option A: card-era write bodies verbatim, actor stays card-derived, **no authority change**); `DecisionSink::commit(principal,…)` inert until PR7 |
| PR6b-1 | #714 | Token **dual-mint** (one secret/one hash/two rows); `card_mcp_tokens` stays sole auth authority, session hash **populate-never-read**; handshake byte-identical; path-scoped CI audit gate |
| PR6b-2 | #717 | HP2 attribution — `PendingEntry.runtime_id`; pending registry now **spawn-keyed** (terminal_id/runtime_id, never card_id); exact-runtime binding; orphan-drop preserved |

**PR7 next** (the keystone): flip MCP handshake + decision-write authority from card-bound to session/`Principal`-bound — reads the `worker_sessions.mcp_token_hash` PR6b-1 has been populating, routes writes through the `CardDecisionSink` seam now gating on `Principal`. Designed/dual-channel-reviewed/ratified before implementation (authority flip = supervised). The original sequence splits this into PR7a (kernel extraction, no authority change) + PR7b (security boundary).

---

## Summary

Separate **execution truth** from **card views**: introduce a `WorkerSession` entity that owns execution identity (MCP token, codex thread, liveness), a `WorkerProvider` trait that extends the existing `ProviderAdapter` saga into the execution period, and a `Principal` security model that removes cards from the authority chain entirely. Cards become pure projections.

## Motivation

> **Code citations — references-as-of.** `file:line` offsets here point at the tree as of the SHA where each threat was first observed (mostly pre-#683 / pre-#689). The *threats* are still real, but line numbers drift as PRs land. Re-grep the function/symbol in the current tree before acting on any offset.

Today the worker card **is** the task's runtime embodiment, and that coupling shows up everywhere:

- `card_mcp_tokens` / `runtimes.card_id` are `ON DELETE CASCADE` from `cards` — deleting a **view** destroys execution **identity** (migrations 0010, 0028).
- The operations saga ends at `spawn_succeeded`; the `SpawnHandle` is dropped on the floor. The execution period is an observability black hole patched by uncoordinated observers (attach_reader, boot scan, harness `persist_snapshot`, adapter compensations).
- No reaper: a worker that dies mid-execution never produces `TaskFailed`; the wave stalls in `Working` with no kernel-side convergence. Only spawn failure has a fallback.
- `role_gate` authority is keyed on card roles via `CardRoleCache`; the spec gate doesn't verify `scope.wave` against the spec card's home wave — it's compensated by emit.rs constructing scope from the card, not guaranteed by the gate.
- Spec is found by scanning cards (`dispatcher::resolve_spec_card`) — a two-hop indirection for what should be a property of the wave.
- Backend behavior can't be tested without minting cards; e2e flakes (daemon-spawn under parallel load, missing codex terminal bytes in CI) trace back to tests forced through real spawn paths.

#594 already moved spec to headless UI — the frontend admits cards are projections; the backend truth is still card-anchored. This issue finishes the thought.

## First principles

Four orthogonal layers; truth lives only below the presentation line:

```
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Presentation    cards / ws streams — projections, subscribers │  optional
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Orchestration   wave FSM + dispatcher + reaper + scheduler    │  deterministic only
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Execution       all agentic sessions (incl. the planner)      │
│                 WorkerSession × WorkerProvider (mechanism)    │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Substrate       operations (sagas) — coordination, NOT truth  │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Truth           state (what IS)  ⊗  events (what HAPPENED)    │
│                 single write entrance, atomically coupled     │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**The truth layer** is two coupled stores: *state* (waves, worker_sessions, coves) answers "what is now"; *events* answer "what happened and why". Four invariants make it real:

- **T1** — every *decision* write commits state + event in one transaction through the single write entrance. (As shipped: `write_with_event`/`write_with_actor_events_typed` is that entrance, with `enforce_role` standing in it. PR4 absorbed the parallel `event_append_for_operation_tx` entrance into the gated `append_decision_event_in_tx<G>` and **deleted** the old fn — a CI grep gate now fails if it reappears.)
- **T2** — *observation* writes (liveness probes, push cursors/watermarks) may update state without emitting events; decision writes never may. Measurements are not journal-worthy. (PR3a made the harness `runtimes.status` an explicit T2 phase-mirror watermark, written through eventless entrances that **deliberately bypass** the status-legality matrix — the harness cycles `idle⇄turn_pending` every turn, edges the frozen matrix denies by design.)
- **T3** — state is **not** `fold(events)`. Consistency comes from transactional coupling, not replay reconstruction. Full event sourcing is an explicit non-goal: event schemas already drift (`codex.job_requested` → `codex.worker_requested` aliases); replay-based testing uses event streams as *notifications*, not the reconstruction basis.
- **T4** — nothing above the substrate reads `operations` as truth. Sagas are in-flight scaffolding; after completion truth is in state + events. (PR4 deleted the parallel `event_append_for_operation_tx` entrance + added a grep firewall; the residual in-tx `operations` reads — e.g. `worker_op_targets_card_tx`'s ownership proof — are coordination breadcrumbs, never operations-as-truth.)

Axioms:

1. **Headless-complete**: every kernel capability is reachable with zero cards. User interaction on a card is a command into the domain; the card updates via projection. One-way loop.
2. **Policy/mechanism split**: the dispatcher decides *what/when*; providers know *how*; `WorkerSession` is where they meet.
3. **Cards are not security principals.** Principals are `User`, `Kernel`, `Agent(session)` — full stop. An agent's grants derive from its session's contract plus the root check, at gate time.
4. **No LLMs above the Execution line.** Orchestration is deterministic kernel machinery only. Everything agentic is a worker: **worker = session × contract × grants**. Contracts are an open set distinguished only by I/O shape — `planner` (observations in, dispatch requests out), `executor` (goal in, result out), `validator` (artifacts + criteria in, verdict out). The spec-card/worker-card split is historical baggage.
5. **The root worker is a recorder.** Each wave designates exactly one root session whose distinguishing grant is wave-state writes (lifecycle + report). Its essence is translating internal system state into externally readable state — the wave lifecycle is an authored interpretation, not a task-count aggregate, which is why an agent (not a counter) writes it. The kernel FSM guards which interpretations are *legal*; the kernel is also the recorder of last resort (auto-promotions, reaper-driven convergence). In practice the root is usually also a planner, but the privilege attaches to recording, not planning.

Names are borrowed from battle-tested systems on purpose: session/controlling-terminal (Unix), spec/status + reconciliation (k8s), principal (security), job/run/attempt (CI).

## Design

### 1. `worker_sessions` — execution truth (flipped successor of `runtimes`)

`runtimes` (0028) is already half a session entity (thread_id, session_id, active_turn_id, handle_state_json, status) — but `card_id NOT NULL REFERENCES cards ON DELETE CASCADE`: truth is a child of the view. The FK is flipped. As shipped (migration 0045, calm-truth):

```sql
CREATE TABLE worker_sessions (
  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  wave_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES waves(id),
  provider TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (provider IN ('codex','claude','terminal')),
  mode TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (mode IN ('ephemeral','resumable')),
  contract TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (contract IN ('planner','executor','validator')),  -- open set, extend by migration
  parent_session_id TEXT NULL REFERENCES worker_sessions(id),       -- delegation tree (≈ ppid)
  requester_session_id TEXT NULL REFERENCES worker_sessions(id),    -- result routing (column live; routing enabled PR11)
  state TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (state IN ('starting','running','idle',
         'turn_pending','exited','failed','superseded')),
  -- execution identity (reclaimed from cards)
  mcp_token_hash TEXT NULL,
  thread_id TEXT NULL, agent_session_id TEXT NULL, active_turn_id TEXT NULL,
  terminal_run_id TEXT NULL REFERENCES terminals(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  handle_state_json TEXT NULL,
  -- liveness (execution-period observation, persisted)
  liveness TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'unknown'
    CHECK (liveness IN ('alive','idle','exited','unknown')),
  liveness_probed_at_ms INTEGER NULL,
  exit_code INTEGER NULL, exit_interpretation TEXT NULL,
  spawn_op_id TEXT NULL REFERENCES operations(id),
  created_at_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, updated_at_ms INTEGER NOT NULL,
  completed_at_ms INTEGER NULL
);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ws_token_idx ON worker_sessions(mcp_token_hash)
  WHERE mcp_token_hash IS NOT NULL;
CREATE INDEX ws_wave_idx ON worker_sessions(wave_id, created_at_ms, id);
CREATE INDEX ws_requester_idx ON worker_sessions(requester_session_id)
  WHERE requester_session_id IS NOT NULL;

ALTER TABLE cards ADD COLUMN session_id TEXT NULL
  REFERENCES worker_sessions(id) ON DELETE SET NULL;   -- view → truth

ALTER TABLE waves ADD COLUMN root_session_id TEXT NULL
  REFERENCES worker_sessions(id);   -- the ROOT planner; O(1), kills resolve_spec_card
```

`session.id == runtime.id` by construction (`RuntimeId`/`WorkerSessionId` are both `String`). **Target state:** deleting a card closes a view (`cards.session_id` → `SET NULL`) and killing a task is an explicit API — but until the PR9b retirement, `card_delete_tx` still cascade-deletes the same-id `worker_sessions` mirror (delete-card-≠-kill is the post-PR9b semantics, not current). Root-ness is **derived** from `wave.root_session_id`, never stored per-row.

### 2. `WorkerProvider` — extend `ProviderAdapter` into the execution period

```rust
pub enum SessionMode { Ephemeral, Resumable }

pub enum Liveness {
    Alive { active_turn_id: Option<String> },
    Idle,
    Exited { evidence: ExitEvidence },
    Unknown { since_ms: TimestampMs },
}

pub struct ExitEvidence {
    pub exit_code: Option<i32>,
    pub signal_killed: bool,
    pub observed_at_ms: TimestampMs,
    pub source: ExitSource,   // AttachReader | Sweeper | Probe | Daemon
}

pub enum ExitInterpretation {
    Completed,
    Failed { reason: String },
    PreserveCard,     // unifies the worker_spawn_failure_preserved semantics
    ResumeEligible,   // Resumable and thread still alive
}

#[async_trait]
pub trait WorkerProvider: Send + Sync {   // standalone as shipped; the issue's original `: ProviderAdapter` supertrait sketch is deferred (see below)
    fn kind(&self) -> &'static str;        // "terminal" | "claude" | "codex" | "fake"
    fn session_mode(&self) -> SessionMode;
    async fn probe_liveness(&self, s: &WorkerSession, ctx: &SpawnCtx) -> Result<Liveness>;
    async fn interpret_exit(&self, s: &WorkerSession, ev: &ExitEvidence,
                            ctx: &SpawnCtx) -> Result<ExitInterpretation>;
    async fn resume(&self, s: &WorkerSession, ctx: &SpawnCtx) -> Result<SpawnHandle> {
        Err(CalmError::Internal(format!("{} not resumable", self.kind())))
    }
}
```

Real impls shipped in **PR6a-1** (`calm-provider`: `TerminalProvider`/`ClaudeProvider`/`CodexProvider` impl `WorkerProvider`), re-exported into `calm-server` but **additive / not yet driven** — the first consumer is the PR8 reaper. No runtime bridge ships yet: `WorkerProvider` and `ProviderAdapter` (the `calm-server` saga-adapter trait) stay **fully separate**, and their discriminators differ (`WorkerProvider::kind()` is `terminal`/`claude`/`codex`; `ProviderAdapter` keys on operation kinds like `codex-worker`/`terminal-create`). Merging the two onto one type (the supertrait/single-type sketch above) is the deferred `provider.rs` TODO: the liveness/exit/resume logic deliberately lives in `calm-provider` (DAG-firewalled below `calm-server`), while `ProviderAdapter` is welded to `calm-server`'s sqlx tx + IO-coupled `SpawnCtx` — the merge waits on abstracting that ctx/dependency shape (post-PR6). `SpawnCtx` stays minimal (`now_ms`); heavyweight deps are construction-time.

**Execution-period state lives on the session, NOT as new `operations.phase` values.** Rationale: `claim_drive_batch` / boot recovery treat every non-terminal phase as a row to drive — an `executing` phase would put every live worker permanently in the drive scan and every boot's recovery plan; the short-lease saga design is mismatched with hours-long execution. The saga *mints* a session; session reaching `running` ⇒ op `succeeded`.

**Probe reality per provider** (PR6a-1): terminal — supervisor `ControlMsg::Probe → ProbeOk{proc_running}`; claude — same PTY probe; codex — **composite evidence only**: PTY probe + daemon `is_running` + the daemon's in-memory active-turn lookup (`active_turn_id_for_thread`) via `CodexDaemonProbe` (calm-server implements the daemon side, breaking the dependency direction), degrading to `Unknown` after daemon restart. The upstream app-server has no thread-status query RPC; a true thread probe needs an upstream RPC addition (verified per the external-protocol rule before assuming).

**Reaper** (PR8, not yet built): a kernel reconciler periodically calls `probe_liveness` on non-terminal sessions; all exit observations funnel through `interpret_exit` as the **single authority**. The arbitration kernel **already exists**: `runtime_status_transition_allowed` + tx-internal CAS + terminal-state absorption (first exit observation wins; the rest are no-ops). Two preconditions: (a) the matrix-bypassing raw UPDATEs are eliminated first (PR3a/PR4 did the absorption; attach_reader funnels at PR8); (b) `interpret_exit` is async and must never run inside the write lock — three-phase: gather evidence (unlocked) → interpret (unlocked) → CAS commit (`WHERE status IN active` + matrix). A dead session with no `TaskCompleted`/`TaskFailed` gets a kernel-emitted `TaskFailed` that flows to the root as a normal observation, letting the wave converge — same path as the existing spawn-failure fallback.

### 3. `Principal` — cards exit the security model

```rust
pub enum Principal {
    User,
    Kernel,    // incl. dispatcher/reaper/scheduler
    Agent { session_id: WorkerSessionId, wave_id: WaveId, cove_id: CoveId },
}
```

An `Agent`'s grants are derived at gate time from its session row: the **contract** (planner/executor/validator) gives the I/O grants, **root-ness** (`session_id == wave.root_session_id`) gives the recorder grant. Nothing is encoded in the token beyond session identity.

- `card_mcp_tokens` → session token: handshake reads token → session row → `Principal`. No card lookup, no `CardRoleCache`. **This flip is PR7** — until then the handshake is byte-identical (daemon-token → `DaemonTrust` short-circuit, else `card_mcp_token_lookup_by_hash` → `CardBound` → `enforce_role`), and the session hash is populate-never-read.
- Decision matrix (enforce + lifecycle merged; agent columns = contract × root-ness):

| operation | User | Kernel | Root (recorder) | Planner (non-root) | Executor / Validator |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| wave lifecycle + report writes | per existing user column | per spec column | per spec column **and wave==w** | deny | deny |
| dispatch (`*.worker_requested`) | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ (wave==w) | ✓ (wave==w) | deny |
| `task.completed`/`task.failed` | ✓ | ✓ | deny | own session only | own session only |
| card projection writes | ✓ | ✓ | own wave | own session | own session |
| hook/message observations | — | ✓ | own wave | own session | own session (carveout dissolves) |

- `wave_lifecycle::validate_transition` edge table unchanged; only the actor-classification function swaps.
- **Closes an existing gap**: the gate today doesn't verify a spec's writes are scoped to its home wave; the root check makes it structural. `EventScope` construction becomes derivable-from-Principal only, making the #232/#234 forged-scope class inexpressible at the type level.

### 4. All agents are workers — contracts, the recorder, the session tree

| contract | input | output (grants) |
|---|---|---|
| `executor` (terminal) | cmd | `task.completed/failed` |
| `executor` (codex/claude) | goal + context | `task.completed/failed` + artifacts |
| `validator` | artifacts/results + acceptance criteria | `task.completed/failed` carrying a verdict |
| `planner` | user messages + observations of its dispatched tasks | `*.worker_requested` |
| *root designation* (orthogonal to contract) | wave-wide observations | lifecycle commands + report edits |

The **root worker is a recorder**: it translates internal system state into externally readable state (wave lifecycle + report). The kernel FSM guards legality; the kernel is the recorder of last resort. Today only the lifecycle half of this monopoly is hard-gated; report writes are soft-gated at the MCP layer — the recorder grant adds report writes to the in-tx gate (PR7), upgrading a soft gate to a structural one.

Consequences:

- **The liveness story closes.** The reaper probes planner/recorder sessions exactly like executors. A stalled/dead root — today's unrecoverable "wave stuck in Working" — becomes reapable with a kernel-side convergence path. The orchestrator-of-last-resort is deterministic kernel machinery, never an LLM.
- **Sub-planners are allowed — at the cost of one real change: result routing.** (Audit correction: results do NOT already route to the requester. Today `TaskCompleted/TaskFailed` route by wave scope → `resolve_spec_card` → the wave's single spec harness; the requester's identity survives only inside `operations.payload_json.actor` — unqueryable.) Required: persist `requester_session_id` (column already in 0045 + indexed) at dispatch time; the push path looks up key → requester with fallback to root; un-bundle the auto-promote side effects from the dispatch tool path. The session tree is `parent_session_id`; a sub-planner observes its own subtree and reports up via `task.completed`. **Non-negotiable**: wave-state write authority belongs to exactly one session at a time, anchored by `wave.root_session_id`. (Enabled in PR11.)
- **Validators close #644's gate.** The verification gate is kernel policy; the verdict is produced by a dispatched `validator` worker — judgment by agent, enforcement by kernel.
- **Orphan semantics** (PR11 refinement): when a sub-planner dies, pending subtree results re-parent to the nearest live ancestor (Unix init-adoption) or the subtree is cascade-killed. Default: re-parent results, cascade-kill still-running dispatches.
- **Delegation guards** (PR11 refinement): depth limit + dispatch budget per subtree.
- **Bootstrap**: the kernel dispatches the root worker on wave start — agents never self-bootstrap. Already true in spirit (`create_wave` mints the spec, a route-side op starts the harness), but a failed start only warns, leaving an inert wave. PR8 brings root start under dispatcher/reaper convergence: a dead-root wave is a reapable condition, not a silent one.
- Aligns #644 (plan-then-schedule): a planner emits a plan as an artifact; the deterministic kernel scheduler executes it.
- Deleted outright (PR7+): `CardRoleCache`, `UnknownCard`/`EmptyAiCardId` guards, AiSpec/AiCodex cross-validation, the spec-card hook carveout, emit.rs per-call card/wave scope back-derivation, `Actor::to_actor_id`'s `AiCodex(CardId(""))` legacy path.

### 5. Cards become projections

| current cards content | verdict |
|---|---|
| id/wave_id/kind/sort/timestamps, `deletable`, icon/theme payload | stays — this *is* the card |
| `role` column (0008) | gone: root via `wave.root_session_id`, everything else via `card.session_id` |
| worker payload: goal/idempotency_key/prompt/`codex_thread_id`/`appserver_sock` | orchestration/identity leakage — moves to session/operation rows |
| spec card kind | deleted (already KernelMintedOnly + unique_per_wave; #594 made it headless) |
| `body_crdt` (wave-report, 0019) | wave-level artifact — moves to wave/report storage |
| terminal/codex/claude kinds | become execution projections subscribing to a session's streams |
| `ui://` plugin kinds | already pure view, untouched |

### 6. Testing pyramid (backend tested with zero frontend)

Injection seams already exist: `Dispatcher::spawn_with_*` constructors, `OperationRuntime::new_unchecked`, `catch_up_push` event injection, the `SharedCodexAppServer` stub mode.

- **L1 orchestration unit tests** (PR5): `FakeProvider` implements `WorkerProvider`, scripted. Because the recorder is also a worker, **FakeRoot** = FakeProvider + a scripted **reaction seam** (the calm-exec `AgentReactor`/`DecisionSink` contract — not a provider-trait side effect; the appserver stub is transport-only and cannot author writes). The in-memory full-loop e2e (`interpret_exit(0)==Completed → TaskCompleted → FakeRoot → DecisionSink commit → wave Done + exactly one WaveLifecycleChanged`, through the real gated entrance) is the structural defense against FakeRoot becoming an unverified abstraction during PR6/PR7 rewrites.
- **L2 wave-FSM tests** (PR5): persist events → `catch_up_push` → assert observations + cursor; no provider, no card.
- **L3 provider conformance** (PR6a-1): one generic `provider_conformance(p: impl WorkerProvider)` run against FakeProvider always; `TerminalProvider`/`ClaudeProvider` as `#[cfg(unix)]` tests; `CodexProvider` behind the `codex-e2e` feature + binary self-skip.
- **L4 frontend**: record FakeProvider-driven event streams as fixtures; replay-based tests become the main path (the playwright `replay --serve` project proves this); real-stack chromium drops to smoke.

If any behavior requires a card to exist before it can be exercised, that's a layering bug (axiom 1).

## Hard problems

Each has a designated PR owner. Implementers MUST re-grep cited symbols before acting (see references-as-of).

1. **`ActorId` is card-shaped and lives in the persisted event log** (`AiSpec(CardId)`/`AiCodex(CardId)`). Migrating identity to sessions means evolving ActorId (event-schema + replay compat) or a session→card alias shim. **Owner: PR10** (PR1 deliberately froze ActorId to keep TS-bindings byte-exact).
2. **Unprompted-card thread attribution race** — RESOLVED (PR6b-2). `codex --remote` cards mint threads on first user input; codex `thread/started` carries **thread_id only — no session/conversation id**, so the FIFO match is the sole binding and `session_id` is derived locally. The pending registry is now **spawn-keyed** (`PendingEntry.runtime_id`/terminal_id, never card_id); `bind_entry` targets the exact registered runtime via `runtime_get_by_id_tx` (missing/superseded/inactive → orphan-drop, never cross-attribution). FIFO + stale-front-drop (0035/0036) preserved.
3. **Single exit authority**: independent state writers funnel through `interpret_exit` or the race just moves into a trait. Absorption owners:
   - `persist_snapshot` raw UPDATE → **PR3a** (T1 status / T2 watermark split) ✅
   - boot recovery scan → **PR3a** (route through entrance) ✅
   - spec-harness adapters' failed/superseded writes → **PR3a** ✅
   - saga-side `event_append_for_operation_tx` callers → **PR4** ✅
   - `attach_reader` runtime-state writes → **PR8** (funnel through `interpret_exit`)
   - adapter compensations (codex fast-exit preserve, worker_cleanup) interpretation route → **PR8**
   - Kernel: the existing transition matrix + tx CAS is the arbitration kernel; preconditions are killing the matrix-bypassing raw UPDATEs (PR3a/PR4 ✅) and keeping `interpret_exit` out of the write lock (three-phase, PR8).
4. **Harness holds concrete types**: `run_loop` held `Arc<SharedCodexAppServer>` (stub/real dual mode); `HarnessRegistry` stored concrete `SpecHarness`. **Owners: PR1 (seam) → PR5 (FakeRoot exercises it via in-memory `DecisionSink`) → PR6 (real harness; codex liveness/exit split behind `CodexProvider`, transport stays in calm-server).** ✅ through PR6.
5. **Worker mint fused into the saga tx**: codex_adapter's `prepare_tx` writes card + terminal + runtime + role cache + events in one tx; compensation keyed by card_id. **Owner: PR6** (provider migration). ✅ — provider impls extracted additively; the spawn saga stays in calm-server, cards staging until PR9.
6. **DaemonTrust threadId path**: per-call identity from client-supplied threadId; the `same_bound_card` cross-check must become `same_bound_session` with no gap. **Owner: PR7** (security boundary), via the transport-driven vector runner.
7. **Planner-tree semantics**: orphaned-subtree policy + delegation guards. **Owner: PR11**.

## Implementation strategy: greenfield crates, not in-place surgery

1. **Shared vocabulary gets its own crate.** Core types (ids, `Principal`, `WorkerContract`, `SessionMode`/`Liveness`, `Event`, `WaveLifecycle`, model DTOs) sink to a bottom-of-DAG `calm-types` crate with no IO deps. Everything speaks the same types from day one. (PR1.)
2. **New layers are fresh crates** — no obligation to reuse calm-server's layout (the deepest card-coupled pieces — dispatcher, role_gate, CardRoleCache — are rewritten, not ported).

Crate boundaries double as **subagent task boundaries and compile firewalls**: `calm-types`/`calm-exec` carry no sqlx/axum, so provider changes stop recompiling kernel tests.

### Crate decomposition (target DAG — `calm-kernel` is PLANNED, does not exist yet)

```
                 calm-server (Presentation shell: routes/ws pump/
                  mcp transport+handshake/plugin_host/replay/
                  card projections/ASSEMBLY: wires all dyn seams;
                  STILL holds the spawn saga, dispatcher, role_gate
                  callers, MCP decision tools until PR7 kernel split)
                    │
              calm-kernel  ── PLANNED (PR7a) ── Orchestration:
               dispatcher/reaper/scheduler/wave FSM/Principal gate impl/
               mcp decision tools (emit, wave_state, wave_report)/
               wave_fs_view/event_cursor
                    │
              calm-provider (codex/claude/terminal real impls,
               CodexDaemonProbe, attach-side exit evidence;
               implements calm-exec traits; uses calm-proc-supervisor)   [PR6a-1]
                    │
              calm-truth (Truth+Substrate: write_with_event single
               entrance/DecisionGate trait (takes &mut WriteTx)/Repo incl.
               worker_sessions/sqlite/migrations/EventBus/saga runtime/
               wave_vcs/role_gate+enforce_role/T1-T4 conformance)         [PR2]
                    │
              calm-exec (Execution contracts, traits ONLY:
               WorkerProvider/SpawnCtx/AgentReactor+DecisionSink/
               ObservationSink; depends only on calm-types)               [PR1]
                    │
              calm-types (vocabulary: ids/Principal/WorkerContract/
               SessionMode/Liveness/WorkerSession entity/Event data
               types/WaveLifecycle/core CoreError — ts-rs exports;
               NO sqlx, NO axum, NO tokio)                                [PR1]
```

Live crates today: `calm-types`, `calm-exec`, `calm-truth`, `calm-provider`, `calm-server`. **`calm-kernel` is planned for PR7a** — until then orchestration (dispatcher, decision tools, role_gate callers) still lives in calm-server. `role_gate.rs`/`mcp_auth.rs` currently live in **calm-truth** (the auth surface the PR6b audit gate scans).

- Acyclicity hinges (verified against the real graph): entities live in types, traits in exec, IO in truth; truth's repos return `calm-types::WorkerSession`; `DecisionGate` is defined in truth and takes `&mut WriteTx` (root check reads `wave.root_session_id` in the same tx — no TOCTOU on root handover); both push directions (`AgentReactor`/`DecisionSink` agent→truth, `ObservationSink` kernel→agent) are exec traits; `CalmError` splits (core → calm-types as `CoreError`; `Db(sqlx::Error)` → calm-truth; `IntoResponse` newtype in calm-server); `event.rs` splits (data/serde/ts-rs → calm-types, `EventBus` → calm-truth).
- Naming: the existing `calm-session` crate is the terminal PTY wire protocol — unrelated; new crates avoid "session" in their names. `calm-proc-supervisor` is provider-only (terminal probe); kernel reaches processes only through exec traits.
- Granularity: a 2-crate cut leaves no FakeProvider firewall; 7–8 crates is coordination overhead. The 6-crate cut is the recommendation.

### PR sequence (gates only assert machinery that exists at that point; every PR has a rollback story)

| PR | nature | content | status |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | tests | Characterization anchor (51 frozen write-entry vectors + freeze gate; event-serde goldens; FSM edge golden; exit-arbitration golden; prod-snapshot replay harness; CASCADE pin; dead-worker-stall L2 pin) | ✅ #683 |
| 1 | new+switch | `calm-types` + `calm-exec` (traits only); ids/Event-data/model/WaveLifecycle moved; Principal/WorkerContract/Liveness/WorkerSession added; `pub use` shims; `gen:api` re-pointed; **no ActorId change** | ✅ #689 |
| 2 | new | `calm-truth`: entrance + sqlite + migrations moved wholesale + `worker_sessions` DDL (0045, incl. `requester_session_id`) + `DecisionGate` (`&mut WriteTx`) + `PermissiveGate` + scoped T1-T4 conformance; single-migrations-dir CI gate | ✅ #697 |
| 3a | switch | raw-UPDATE absorption round 1 (harness side): persist_snapshot / boot recovery / spec-harness failed-superseded raw status → eventless calm-truth entrances; harness status = T2 watermark; **no `worker_sessions` touch** | ✅ #703 |
| 3b | switch | `runtimes`↔`worker_sessions` dual-write in one tx (`derive_session_identity`, id-keyed) + boot backfill + 3-layer parity. Split: **3b-i** (#705 dual-write + Layer-1/2) + **3b-ii** (#706 Layer-3 env-gated boot diff) | ✅ #705/#706 |
| 4 | switch | raw event-append absorption round 2 (saga side): 9 `event_append_for_operation_tx` callers → gated `append_decision_event_in_tx<G>` (`&PermissiveGate`); parallel entrance deleted; T4 firewall + CI gate | ✅ #707 |
| 5 | new | FakeProvider + FakeRoot + L1/L2 harness + in-memory `DecisionSink` + full-loop e2e (the structural defense for FakeRoot through PR6/PR7); `GatedDecisionSink` test-only defender | ✅ #708 |
| 6 | migrate + security | `calm-provider` + reaction seam + token dual-mint + HP2. Shipped as **4 sub-PRs**: **6a-1** (#710 provider impls), **6a-2** (#713 `CardDecisionSink`, **no authority change**), **6b-1** (#714 token dual-mint, populate-never-read), **6b-2** (#717 HP2 spawn-keyed attribution) | ✅ #710/#713/#714/#717 |
| 7a | new+switch | `calm-kernel` extraction: dispatcher rewritten against `WorkerProvider`; MCP decision tools move to kernel; sweeper retired. **Legacy Actor model + CardRoleCache preserved — no security-boundary change.** | next |
| 7b | new+switch | **Security boundary**: Principal gate (`&mut WriteTx`-derivative, in-tx root check) + `wave.root_session_id` backfill + token authority flips to sessions (handshake reads `worker_sessions.mcp_token_hash`; populate-never-read window closes) + transport-driven vector runner + frozen/characterization vector split | planned |
| 8 | new | reaper + `interpret_exit` single exit authority + root-start unification (dead root = reapable); attach_reader writes funnel through `interpret_exit` | planned |
| 9a | switch+migrate | read-flip + `calm-codex-bridge` identity migration (session_id ingest, dual-emit compat window); all reads `runtimes` → `worker_sessions` (runtimes still written — rollback-safe) | planned |
| 9b | switch | retirement (irreversible — schema rollback ends here): drop `runtimes`/`card_mcp_tokens`/CardRoleCache/spec card kind; cardless sessions; delete-card-≠-kill; bridge legacy `?card_id=` retired | planned |
| 10 | new | ActorId evolution (HP1) + event-log replay compat | planned |
| 11 | follow-up | sub-planner dispatch enabled (`requester_session_id` schema ready since PR2) + orphan/budget policies (HP7) | planned |

> **PR7 note:** the latest status framing treats "PR7" as the single keystone authority flip; the design-of-record above splits it into 7a (kernel extraction, no authority change) + 7b (security boundary). Either way, 7b is the slice where token→session authority becomes load-bearing.

**PR1 shim categories**: two patterns coexist — (a) **full pass-through** (`pub use calm_types::ids;`) for purely-data types, kept until PR9b/PR11; (b) **partial shim module** for DTOs still depending on sqlx/utoipa-axum, emptying out as dependent crates land.

### Invariant preservation — how each stage is guaranteed

Three mechanisms carry the sequence (the PR gates are point assertions; this is the systematic answer to "what keeps the system stable *through* it"):

1. **Frozen security vectors** (PR0; two-layer corpus from PR7b). The decision matrix as data files (`crates/calm-server/tests/vectors/gate_denials/*.json`: event kind × actor × scope → allow/deny). **Critical precision**: PR0's runner is **write-entry black-box** (driven through `Repo::log_pure_event`), NOT transport black-box — it does not exercise MCP/HTTP handshake, `_meta.threadId`, tool routing, or request-side scope. Cells whose semantics live in transport (cross-session threadId, `same_bound_session`) require the **transport-driven companion runner** added in PR7b. CI fails any commit touching the vectors dir without a `FROZEN-VECTOR-CHANGE:` rationale. PR0 ships **51** write-entry vectors; PR7b adds the transport runner + delta vectors + flips the characterization surprises (`AiSpec→task.completed=allow`, ReportCard no-self-scope-check) into the frozen set.
2. **Test-against-trait conformance suites** — generic fns (`gate_conformance`, `provider_conformance`, T1–T4) in calm-truth/calm-exec dev-deps; the legacy impl runs the same suite during the dual-implementation window. Scoped narrowly at PR2 (calm-truth APIs only); PR3a brought harness paths into T1/T2; PR4 brought saga paths into T1.
3. **Parity, three layers** (PR3b): (a) dual-write in one tx + teardown full-table diff — every integration test becomes a parity test for free; (b) production-side periodic background diff (`tracing::warn!` + counter, **not** a wire Event); (c) boot-time full diff as the PR9b retirement precondition (env-gated, default OFF). `debug_assert` is explicitly not a production mechanism.

### Greenfield-specific risks

1. **Dual-track consistency (PR3b–9a)**: `runtimes` + `worker_sessions` coexist. Mitigation: dual-write only inside the calm-truth single entrance's tx; standing parity assertion; boot-scan diff before retirement.
2. **Migration-chain ownership transfer**: a leftover `migrate!` in calm-server = dual sources, checksum refusals. Mitigation: PR2 moved the chain wholesale + CI "exactly one migrations/ in workspace" gate + replay against a prod snapshot.
3. **TS export chain breakage**: `gen:api` dispatches by crate name while `TS_RS_EXPORT_DIR` is workspace-root. Mitigation: PR1 updated web/package.json in the same change.
4. **Shim-window type drift**: Mitigation: PR1 deleted source definitions (shims `pub use` only) + CI grep against re-declarations.
5. **Token authority window (PR6–7b)**: the `card_mcp_tokens` table and the additive `worker_sessions.mcp_token_hash` column hold the same hash. Mitigation: `card_mcp_tokens` is the **sole auth authority** until the PR7b flip; the `worker_sessions` hash is **never read on the auth path** (no by-hash lookup; the column is only hydrated by non-auth session reads/tests), enforced by a **path-scoped CI audit gate** (scans `mcp_server/` + `calm-truth/role_gate.rs` + `mcp_auth.rs`, bans `worker_sessions`/`mcp_token_hash`/`session_mcp_token`/`agent_session_id`). Rollback to any pre-PR6 binary keeps running workers' MCP alive (the auth path reads only the card table, or the daemon-token `DaemonTrust` short-circuit — never the session table; proven by a live rollback test corrupting the session hash to garbage, identity still resolves).
6. **Bridge version skew**: `calm-codex-bridge` deploys inside codex homes and upgrades out of band; keys hooks on `NEIGE_CARD_ID` today. Mitigation: PR9a's dual-emit window + skew test matrix; cardless sessions (PR9b) cannot land before PR9a (structurally enforced by PR9a→9b order).

## Non-goals

- No change to the Event wire protocol (`*.worker_requested` / `task.completed` / `task.failed` stay).
- No change to the wave lifecycle FSM edges or the user/spec permission matrix semantics.
- No multi-trait-per-task-type abstraction: one trait, capabilities via `SessionMode`/contracts/grants.
- No dissolution of the recorder monopoly: sub-planners exist, but wave-state write authority is anchored to `wave.root_session_id`, exactly one session at a time.
- No full event sourcing: state is not rebuilt by folding events (T3); the event log is an atomically-coupled fact journal + notification stream.

title: [R1N Gate] XuanLing Core Hardening and Runtime Consolidation
raw_text:
[R1N Gate] XuanLing Core Hardening and Runtime Consolidation

## Routing

Window: MotherTree / XuanLing Core Hardening
Gate: Yellow
Status: structural consolidation gate; review-only
Return_Path: GitHub issue -> MotherTree review -> core hardening map -> optional registry/KB/file cleanup

## Core

XuanLing has moved beyond its initial concept state. It is no longer only a prompt structure, model memory chain, or platform-specific workflow. Recent tests have shown that the architecture can operate across:

- GitHub / Linear task pipe
- GitHub -> Qinyi public-surface translation pipe
- MCP / API adapter boundary
- platform task/project/workflow surface reading
- universal generate-refine-calibrate chain
- Lightblue closed-environment manual-gate package
- human-gated assistant workflow under restricted enterprise conditions

Therefore, the next work should not continue as scattered feature additions. It should harden XuanLing into a precise runtime architecture.

## Key Reframe

```text
XuanLing is not a model, not a platform, and not a collection of tools.
XuanLing is a spatial-chain operating architecture that turns multi-cloud, multi-tool, multi-role, multi-carrier work into gated, traceable, returnable, and reconstructable chains.
```

## Why This Gate Is Needed

Current repository risk:

```yaml
Risk:
  - too many registers without clear hierarchy
  - issues growing faster than consolidation
  - scheduler/window concepts overlapping
  - Lightblue package mistaken as general system
  - MCP/API mistaken as absolute interface
  - GitHub mistaken as ontology instead of registry/review surface
  - XuanLing described in fragments rather than hardened runtime layers
```

The architecture has already been tested enough to justify consolidation.

## Runtime Reading v0.1

```yaml
XuanLing_Core_Runtime:
  L0_Invariant_Core:
    role: non-drifting center; defines what cannot be changed
    includes:
      - invariant core
      - axis
      - purpose
      - boundary

  L1_Spatial_Chain_Field:
    role: relation-space where clouds, tools, people, models, files, and tasks become nodes
    includes:
      - cloud-over-cloud
      - spatial-chain ecosystem
      - route rights
      - node relations

  L2_Rail_and_Round_System:
    role: keeps work from becoming disconnected generations
    includes:
      - task card
      - round card
      - previous-next adhesion
      - one round / one slice

  L3_Gate_and_Boundary_System:
    role: prevents misuse, overreach, leakage, billing/runtime drift, and unsupported claims
    includes:
      - Green / Yellow / Red gate
      - no-billing / no-runtime
      - security / permission boundary
      - Fact / Inference / Pending

  L4_Carrier_and_Adapter_Layer:
    role: treats platforms and tools as replaceable carriers, not the system body
    includes:
      - GitHub
      - Linear
      - Lightblue
      - OneDrive
      - M365
      - API / MCP / OAuth / document packets
      - human gate

  L5_Output_and_Refinement_Loop:
    role: turns first-generation outputs into stable deliverables through review and calibration
    includes:
      - generate
      - review
      - refine
      - calibrate
      - regenerate

  L6_Return_and_Rebuild_Layer:
    role: ensures outputs return to the right registry, decision point, or next task
    includes:
      - Return Packet
      - registry
      - closeout
      - archive
      - edge rebuild
```

## Separation From Ordinary Cognition

XuanLing should not be explained as a normal assistant workflow.

```yaml
Not_Enough:
  - prompt template
  - project management
  - workflow automation
  - model memory
  - MCP/API integration
  - GitHub repo organization
  - Lightblue assistant package

Actual_Frame:
  - relation-space routing
  - route-rights layer
  - human/model/tool/carrier chain governance
  - bounded generation and refinement loop
  - returnable and reconstructable runtime
```

## Tested Evidence From Recent Rounds

```yaml
Validated_Signals:
  R1J:
    - GitHub_to_Linear Task_Pipe
    - GitHub_to_Qinyi_Public_Surface Translation_Pipe

  R1K:
    - Universal Generate-Refine-Calibrate Chain

  R1L:
    - MCP/API are adapter surfaces, not system ontology

  R1M:
    - Lightblue cannot be treated as a workflow system
    - Lightblue is a restricted generation assistant node
    - human-gated assistant workflow is the minimal viable enterprise form

  Platform_Surface_Reading:
    - planning/task/workflow words are surface signals, not commands
```

## Consolidation Objectives

```yaml
Objectives:
  1_Define_Core_Layers:
    output: one hardened runtime layer map

  2_Clean_Registry_Hierarchy:
    output: define which register is master, which is index, which is role table, which is archive

  3_Separate_Scheduler_From_Window_Frame:
    output: 12-window = runtime frame; 00-04 scheduler topology = cadence governance

  4_Clarify_Carrier_vs_System:
    output: GitHub/Lightblue/API/MCP/OneDrive are carriers/adapters only

  5_Reclassify_Lightblue:
    output: Lightblue package becomes one restricted-enterprise playbook, not universal core

  6_Create_Core_Hardening_Map:
    output: XUANLING_CORE_RUNTIME_HARDENING_MAP.md candidate
```

## Immediate Cleanup Guidance

Before adding new feature files, repository cleanup should prioritize:

```yaml
Cleanup_Order:
  1: establish master registry hierarchy
  2: update discontinuity statuses that are already addressed
  3: mark overlapping registers as index / artifact / role / cleanup instead of competing masters
  4: mark daily generic schedule as deprecated or absorbed into CVG_3D
  5: create one hardening map instead of many small doctrine files
```

## Proposed New Artifact

```yaml
Candidate_File:
  path: XUANLING_CORE_RUNTIME_HARDENING_MAP.md
  purpose:
    - define XuanLing as platform-independent spatial-chain runtime
    - consolidate recent tests into one durable architecture map
    - prevent future drift into tool/platform/model-specific explanations
  status: candidate only until MotherTree review
```

## Do Not

```yaml
Do_Not:
  - do not keep adding disconnected feature issues
  - do not treat GitHub as the system ontology
  - do not treat Lightblue package as universal core
  - do not treat MCP/API as absolute path
  - do not rewrite all existing files at once
  - do not merge/close prior issues automatically
  - do not expose company or private data
```

## Review Questions

1. Should the next repository action be a single `XUANLING_CORE_RUNTIME_HARDENING_MAP.md`?
2. Which files are master registry vs supporting register?
3. Should R1M be reclassified as `Restricted Enterprise Playbook`?
4. Should 12-window and 00-04 scheduler be explicitly separated?
5. Which prior issues should be marked as supporting signals rather than active development lanes?
6. How do we keep the architecture thick but not bloated?

## Acceptance Criteria

```yaml
Acceptance_Criteria:
  - XuanLing is defined beyond model/platform/tool memory
  - recent tests are consolidated into durable layers
  - carrier vs core distinction is explicit
  - repository cleanup direction is clear
  - no confidential or company data is included
  - next action is one hardening map, not many scattered additions
```

## Return Packet

```yaml
Window: MotherTree / XuanLing Core Hardening
Task_ID: R1N_XUANLING_CORE_HARDENING
What_Changed:
  - opened structural consolidation gate for XuanLing runtime hardening
What_Did_Not_Change:
  - no files rewritten yet
  - no PR created
  - no issues closed
  - no company/private data used
Risk:
  - architecture may bloat if every insight becomes a separate file
Pending:
  - MotherTree decision on creating XUANLING_CORE_RUNTIME_HARDENING_MAP.md
Next_Action:
  - produce one hardening map and then patch only the minimum required registers
Return_Path: GitHub issue -> MotherTree review -> hardening map -> minimal registry cleanup
```

- HR / hiring: `personalized-interview-simulator.ts`
- Competitive analysis: `competitive-monitoring.ts`
- Incident response: `incident-postmortem-dag.ts`
- Productivity: `meeting-summarizer.ts`
- Quality / cross-model: `translation-backtranslation.ts`

If your idea maps onto one of these, it's shipped.

## The bar

Four conditions, all required:

1. Domain not in the list above.
2. Someone outside your friend group would realistically Google this.
3. The run produces something a human can act on (a report, decision, plan), not just "completed successfully".
4. Each agent reads a genuinely different source, and the demo surfaces a real conflict the arbiter resolves. Three pre-aligned drafts being merged is not conflict resolution.

If you're unsure your proposal clears all four, it probably doesn't. Reshape before commenting.

## Proposal format

> **Background**: domain you've spent real time in
>
> **Pain point**: concrete pain you've felt, not "industry X uses AI"
>
> **Search query**: what someone would Google to land on this example
>
> **Output artifact**: what the user gets at the end, one line
>
> **Design**: agents, what source each reads, OMA primitives (`runTeam` / `runTasks` / shared memory / structured output), and the conflict the arbiter resolves
>
> **Sources**: one line per source, flagged MOCK or LIVE

## What we pass on

Domain overlap with the eight examples. Hobby use cases. Standard chatbot / RAG / support-bot demos. Designs where all agents query the same LLM's internal knowledge. Designs without a real runtime conflict. Proposals missing your background.

---

## 1. Ecosystem Overview

The open-source AI agent ecosystem on 2026-06-16 is characterized by **high infrastructure fragmentation** and **converging architectural pressures** across at least 12 active projects. No project released a versioned build today, indicating industry-wide accumulation of breaking changes before coordinated release cycles. The dominant pattern is **orchestration-layer maturation**: projects are racing to solve context window management, tool-use reliability, and multi-agent delegation while remaining downstream of proprietary model providers. Vision-language capabilities remain **nascent and unevenly distributed**—only IronClaw shipped substantive multimodal infrastructure today, while most projects handle non-text inputs through brittle plumbing rather than integrated reasoning. ## 7. Trend Signals

### 7.1 Infrastructure-Induced Hallucinations Are Emerging as a Distinct Failure Class
**Evidence**: NanoBot #4345 (image-strip fallback creates false perception); ZeroClaw #7741 (multimodal cache poisoning); OpenClaw #25592 (tool reasoning leaks to user channels).

**Value for developers**: Model weights are not the sole hallucination source. **Orchestration-layer fallbacks**—designed to be "helpful"—can synthesize false evidence. Defensive design requires **explicit failure markers** (`[unviewable]`, `ErrorResult`) rather than synthetic substitutions.

### 7.2 Reasoning Parameter Fragmentation Demands Abstraction Layers
**Evidence**: NanoBot #4351 (Mistral `reasoning_effort` strictness vs. OpenAI four-tier scale); ZeroClaw #7725/#7616 (provider-specific reasoning content handling).

**Value for developers**: Proliferating reasoning models with incompatible control surfaces will strain unified agent frameworks. **Standardized reasoning controls** (effort, visibility, chain-of-thought format) are a likely standardization battleground.

### 7.3 Context Compression Is Becoming User-Facing and Research-Critical
**Evidence**: CoPaw #5063 (Headroom 60–95% compression); ZeroClaw #7673 (compression decorator RFC); OpenClaw #22438 (progressive loading); Hermes #41624 (compression hooks).

**Value for developers**: Compression is transitioning from **transparent optimization** to **explicit user concern**. Projects with verified, reversible, semantically-aware compression will have measurable trust and reproducibility advantages. **Instrumentation integrity** (displayed vs. actual tokens) is a prerequisite for empirical research.

### 7.4 Tiered Inference (Fast Classification → Slow Execution) Is Community-Driven
**Evidence**: ZeroClaw #6067 (light model reply-intent precheck with timeout telemetry); Hermes #41626 (MoA routing with provider-aware reasoning-disable).

**Value for developers**: Cost-latency pressures are pushing **speculative reasoning architectures** into open-source agent frameworks. Projects enabling systematic A/B of model tiers for routing decisions will support research on **cascading reasoning** and **early-exit efficiency**.

### 7.5 Silent Failures Systematically Undermine AI Reliability Research
**Evidence**: NanoClaw #2759 (dropped error turns); CoPaw #5161 (silent hangs); PicoClaw #3130 (silent JSON marshal failures); OpenClaw #29387 (silent bootstrap ignore).

**Value for developers**: **Observability-first design** is not optional for research-validated systems. Every failure mode must be **materialized as a structured object** in the interaction trace, not swallowed or dropped. Projects lacking this pattern will be excluded from rigorous reliability studies.

## Research Analyst Notes

**Key observations for multimodal reasoning and AI reliability research:**

1. **Hallucination from system-level fallbacks** (#4345/#4346): This is a concrete instance of **infrastructure-induced hallucination** — not model weights, but the orchestration layer creating false perceptual evidence. The fix (marking `[unviewable]`) is a minimal intervention; researchers should consider whether more explicit "modality failure" signals would improve model calibration.

2. **Token-vs-character context capping** (#4352): The shift from character to token boundaries reflects maturation in context window management. CJK and code-heavy contexts were previously underrepresented; this has implications for **multilingual reasoning evaluation fairness**.

3. **Reasoning parameter fragmentation** (#4351): Mistral's `reasoning_effort` accepting only `"high"` or `"none"` versus OpenAI's four-tier scale exemplifies **emerging API divergence in reasoning controls**. Standardization pressure will likely increase as reasoning models proliferate.

4. **Replay-window integrity** (#4348, #4349): The repeated attention to "where to cut" in long contexts suggests **turn-boundary-aware compaction** is non-trivial. This is relevant to long-context benchmark design — naive truncation strategies may destroy reasoning chains invisibly.

Most ETFs and mutual funds today are not that complicated - they can be expressed as a CSV file with 2 columns - a ticker and a share number. You can find these holding csv files on most ETF pages (VOO[2], QQQ[3]). Right now there are about $9.1T of assets in ETFs[4] and $20T in Mutual Funds[5] in the US, with estimated revenue of $100B per year. We think this market is ripe for disruption.

We offer 50+ strategies that track popular ETFs and are updated as stocks merge and indexes change. You can customize these by weighting sectors or stocks differently, or even build your own indexes from scratch using our stock/etf screening tools. Once you've chosen your strategy, simply set your target weights and deposit funds (we also support transferring existing stocks). Our engine then checks your portfolio daily for potential trades, optimizes for tax-loss harvesting, portfolio tracking, and redeploys any generated cash.

I (JJ) started working on this after selling my last company. After using nearly every brokerage product out there and working with a financial advisor, I noticed a huge gap between the indexing capabilities of financial advisors and what individual investors could access. We wanted to bridge that gap and provide these powerful tools to everyone in a simple, low-cost way.

There are a number of robo-advisor products out there, but none that we know of offer direct indexing without expense ratios or AUM fees. One similar product is M1 Finance, but Double is more powerful. We offer tax-loss harvesting, a wider range of indexes, and greater customization. For example, when building your own index, you can set weights down to 0.1% (compared to M1's 1%) and even weight by market cap.

We also compete with robo-advisors like Wealthfront, but offer more control over your investments. And did I mention we don't charge AUM fees? You can see our strategies and play with the research page https://double.finance/p/explore without creating an account.

Over the past year we’ve learned a lot about the guts of building portfolio software. For example, stocks don’t really have persistent identifiers that are easy to model and pass around. We trade CUSIPs with our custodian Apex*, but these change all the time for stock splits or re-org’s that you would not think would lead to a new “stock”.

We’ve also learned a lot about how tax loss harvesting (TLH) is best implemented on large direct index portfolios using a factor model as opposed to pairs based replacements which I initially thought might be the way to execute these. We do use a pairs strategy on smaller sized strategies. And how TLH and portfolio optimization generally is best expressed as a linear optimization problem with competing objectives (tracking vs. tax alpha vs. trading costs for example).

If you have any thoughts on the product or our positioning as the low fee alternative I’d love to hear it. I think Robinhood has proved that you can build a strong business by getting rid of an industry wide cost (in their case commissions, in our expense ratios). We aim to do the same.

DarkSouls - PT and NRD

Hello Dzhdan,

Thanks for all your support so far. As discussed we can use this consolidated thread from here on. I will start with this template so is easier.

Problem Statement : 
1. Passing Confidence inputs to NRD - Reblur so that it can disocclude regions of shading change temporally. Most noticeable with Shadows of Moving/Animated objects when Reblur is used to denoise Direct and Indirect lighting together from LocalLightSources (Point/Spot/Area Lights)

Solution Plan: 
1. During SHARC Rendering(5x5 Downscale). Output the following properties Visibility Buffer - HitInstance, PrimitiveId, Radiance Buffer Raw. This pass technically need not be with SHARC, but is useful to combine
2. Fetch Previous Buffers output from 1(Visibility buffer, Radiance). GetPosition in PreviousFrame, Run the path tracer loop again, note we already know the previous frame seed used. Compared the results and output to a buffer.
3. Blur the Output from 2 multiple times, do a 1 frame temporal accumulation with Confidence Output Buffer from Previous. Finally Upscale the output to full resolution(Bilinear), which will be confidence input to NRD.


PS : Maybe I can reuse the 2nd path trace loop to update the SharcCache as well. Improving cache quality. As the SHARC cache operates in world space

Let me know what you think of my plan.

title: The future of content filtering (declarativeNetRequest, Manifest v3, and beyond)
raw_text:
The future of content filtering (declarativeNetRequest, Manifest v3, and beyond)

This is both an FYI and some follow-on questions.

The FYI -- For those who haven't yet heard, Google is planning a severe reduction in extension capability for blockers and other content filters. Their current draft of changes includes deprecating the webRequest API and replacing it with declarativeNetRequest. This will only permit a fixed number of purely declaritive rules in a single json list. Moreover, the browser will have final say on what requests get blocked or redirected.

For more info, see [this uBlock Origin thread](https://github.com/uBlockOrigin/uBlock-issues/issues/338). It has all of the relevant links.

I have two follow-on questions:

1. Is there any interest from the developers here to integrate a filtering engine?  I realize this is a big request, but the new API will eliminate the possibility of uBlock Origin, uMatrix, and other robust extensions. Since this project recommends those on the wiki, it will impact this project and its users. My idea is to modify [Brave's engine](https://github.com/brave/ad-block), which is already integrated but has only AdBlock Plus level functionality.

2. If not, can you recommend how to undertake such an effort?  I have experience working with large C++ codebases, but nothing browser-related. Any tips, gotchas, etc. would be appreciated.

title: PRD: Migrate agents to Pydantic AI (adapter-first) — umbrella
raw_text:
PRD: Migrate agents to Pydantic AI (adapter-first) — umbrella

# PRD: Pydantic AI Migration (adapter-first)

> Umbrella PRD. Design doc: [`docs/design/langchain-pydantic-ai-migration.md`](langchain-pydantic-ai-migration.md)
>
> Near-term reality is **Pydantic AI + Monty Code Mode**. LangChain is a deferred, optional remote-sandbox backend only — it does **not** own code-mode.

## Problem Statement

MCP-Universe maintains a custom agent and LLM framework (BaseLLM, BaseAgent, hand-rolled ReAct and function-call loops, YAML-driven WorkflowBuilder, ComponentABCMeta registry). While functional and benchmark-proven, this stack is difficult for new contributors to learn because patterns are project-specific rather than aligned with widely adopted open-source ecosystems. Three parallel agent stacks already exist (`BaseLLM` agents, `OpenAIAgentSDK`, `ClaudeCodeAgent`) plus `TITOLLMWrapper` for RL, each bypassing the common contract differently.

The framework also faces growing context-window pressure from verbose MCP tool outputs. Multiple overlapping mitigation mechanisms exist today (MCP+, `summarize_tool_response`, in-process `SafeCodeExecutor`, `python-code-sandbox` Docker MCP), and there is no unified strategy for programmatic tool calling (code-mode).

The team needs a maintainable path to adopt **Pydantic AI** for agent runtime and context reduction — while continuing to support OpenAI, Azure, OpenRouter, and (later) local LLMs (vllm_local / sglang_local) — without breaking existing benchmarks, YAML configs, or trace/report outputs.

## Solution

Adopt an **adapter-first migration**: Pydantic AI becomes the primary agent runtime; the existing MCPClient layer, BenchmarkRunner, evaluators, env_pool, and tracing remain the source of truth with thin adapters on top.

New Pydantic AI-backed agent and LLM classes **claim the existing YAML `type:` aliases via the component registry** (registry swap); the legacy implementations are renamed to `*_legacy` aliases and kept for rollback and comparison. Benchmark configs require no edits.

Context reduction is layered: **Pydantic AI Code Mode (Monty)** is the primary programmatic-tool-calling mechanism for capable models, and **MCP+ remains as a model-agnostic fallback** for single oversized tool payloads. The two are complementary, not competing.

Deliverable for the analysis task: **design document + POC** proving one benchmark domain runs end-to-end on the new stack.

## User Stories

1. As a **framework maintainer**, I want agents implemented on Pydantic AI, so that new contributors can use familiar OSS patterns instead of learning custom BaseAgent loops.

2. As a **framework maintainer**, I want a single internal LLM provider factory covering OpenAI-family providers (openai, azure, openrouter, and OpenAI-compatible local endpoints), so that adding or switching providers does not require duplicate agent code.

3. As a **benchmark operator**, I want existing YAML benchmark configs to work unchanged, so that CI and Azure benchmark scripts do not break mid-migration.

4. As a **benchmark operator**, I want BenchmarkRunner, Task evaluators, and BenchmarkReport to work without modification, so that evaluation infrastructure investment is preserved.

5. As a **benchmark operator**, I want trace files and report output to remain compatible with current tooling, so that historical comparison and MCP+ tracer analysis still work.

6. As a **research engineer**, I want function_call agents migrated to Pydantic AI first, so that the most YAML-common agent type proves the adapter pattern quickly.

7. As a **research engineer**, I want react agents migrated for models without reliable native tool calling, so that local-LLM benchmarks remain viable in a later phase.

8. As a **research engineer**, I want wide research agents migrated, so that the flagship parallel tool-calling feature stays on the maintained stack.

9. As a **research engineer**, I want MCP tools exposed to Pydantic AI agents via adapters over the existing MCPClient, so that permissions, gateway routing, and env_pool integration are not reimplemented.

10. As a **research engineer**, I want tool names to remain in the `server__tool` convention, so that existing evaluators and task definitions stay valid.

11. As a **context-cost owner**, I want a unified context reduction layer, so that Code Mode and MCP+ are composed deliberately instead of competing ad hoc mechanisms.

12. As a **context-cost owner**, I want Code Mode / programmatic tool calling via Pydantic AI (Monty sandbox) for supported models, so that agents can call tools in code and only return final results to chat history.

13. As a **context-cost owner**, I want MCP+ as a model-agnostic fallback for single oversized tool payloads, so that large one-shot outputs are still compressed at the MCP transport layer even when Code Mode is unavailable.

14. As a **context-cost owner**, I want MCP+ `PostProcessAgent` refactored onto Pydantic AI, so that the extension is maintainable alongside the new agent stack.

15. As a **security-conscious operator**, I want env_pool to continue provisioning isolated Docker MCP Gateway environments, so that Playwright, Postgres, and Blender tasks remain properly isolated.

16. As a **security-conscious operator**, I want Code Mode to run in the Monty in-process sandbox (no filesystem/network/env access), so that generated Python cannot escape to the host.

17. As a **security-conscious operator**, I want a hybrid execution strategy, so that MCP-heavy benchmarks use env_pool, code-mode uses Monty, and general Python execution uses the existing `python-code-sandbox` MCP.

18. As a **local LLM user**, I want vllm_local and sglang_local supported via OpenAI-compatible Pydantic AI providers in a later phase, so that local inference does not require separate agent implementations.

19. As an **OpenRouter user**, I want openrouter supported via the same provider factory, so that model routing stays configuration-driven.

20. As an **OpenAI / Azure user**, I want openai and azure providers supported, so that cloud benchmark scripts (e.g. Azure benchmarks) continue to work.

21. As an **RL engineer**, I want RL, TITO, and VERL integration to remain on the legacy stack during early phases, so that the OSS migration does not block training workflows.

22. As a **workflow author**, I want custom orchestration workflows (chain, router, orchestrator) to remain on the legacy stack initially, so that migration scope stays bounded.

23. As a **contributor writing tests**, I want the POC validated by an existing benchmark integration test, so that viability is proven by external behavior not unit mocks.

24. As a **contributor writing tests**, I want provider/agent tests following existing test patterns, so that test style stays consistent.

25. As a **contributor writing tests**, I want registry resolution tested so legacy `type:` aliases instantiate the Pydantic AI implementations, so that YAML compatibility is regression-protected.

26. As a **project lead**, I want a phased roadmap split into independently reviewable child issues, so that work can be parallelised and reviewed in small PRs.

27. As a **project lead**, I want an analysis deliverable (design doc + working POC), so that stakeholders can sign off before full implementation.

28. As a **downstream integrator**, I want the Executor contract (`execute` → AgentResponse) preserved, so that FastAPI app and pipeline launcher integrations do not break.

29. As an **MCP+ user**, I want `mcp-build-plus` CLI and wrapper configs to keep working, so that Cursor/Claude Code integrations are not disrupted during the MCP+ refactor.

30. As a **future maintainer**, I want legacy BaseLLM/BaseAgent types kept as `*_legacy` aliases rather than deleted immediately, so that rollback and gradual migration are possible.

## Implementation Decisions

### Strategy

- **Adapter-first, not rewrite.** Approximately 70% of the codebase (MCP layer, benchmarks, evaluators, env_pool, tracing) stays; agent loops, the internal LLM provider factory, and context middleware are the rewrite surface.
- **Pydantic AI owns the agent runtime and code-mode.** LangChain is **not** adopted as a second agent framework and does **not** own code-mode; it is a deferred, optional remote-sandbox backend only.

### YAML compatibility — registry swap (not transparent routing)

- New Pydantic AI-backed classes **claim the existing aliases** through the `ComponentABCMeta` registry: e.g. the new function-call agent registers alias `function_call`; the legacy class is renamed to `function_call_legacy`.
- Same pattern for the LLM layer: the new Pydantic AI-backed model claims `azure` (and later `openai`, `openrouter`); legacy classes become `azure_legacy`, etc.
- No WorkflowBuilder special-case routing table. No external YAML changes. Rollback = point YAML `type:` at the `*_legacy` alias.

### LLM provider factory

- An internal provider factory builds a Pydantic AI model for OpenAI-family providers (openai, azure, openrouter, and OpenAI-compatible local endpoints) behind the claimed aliases.
- POC proves `azure` (the provider `financial_analysis.yaml` currently uses). openai/openrouter follow in Phase 1.
- Local providers (vllm_local/sglang_local) are deferred to their own phase.

### Agent migration

- **POC:** function_call only, `azure` provider.
- **Phase 1:** react and wide research agents; openai + openrouter providers.
- Agents implement the existing Executor contract; internally delegate to a Pydantic AI Agent with MCP toolsets.

### MCP integration

- MCPClient and MCPManager remain source of truth.
- A new adapter layer converts MCPClient tools into Pydantic AI tool definitions (delegating execution to `execute_tool`) **without** replacing transport, permissions, gateway, or env_pool logic.
- The `server__tool` naming convention is preserved at the adapter boundary.

### Context layer

- **Primary:** Pydantic AI Code Mode via `pydantic-ai-harness[code-mode]` (Monty sandbox) — wraps tools into a single `run_code` tool; MCP tools wrapped with `native=False` so they route through the local toolset and into the sandbox.
- **Fallback:** MCP+ wrapper for single oversized tool payloads and models that cannot do code-mode.
- The duplicate `summarize_tool_response` paths on legacy agents are deprecated over time in favour of this layer. MCP+ itself is **kept**.

### Sandboxes / execution (hybrid)

- **env_pool:** unchanged for benchmark and RL MCP Gateway isolation.
- **Monty:** in-process sandbox for Code Mode (no fs/network/env).
- **`python-code-sandbox` MCP:** remains for general Docker-isolated Python execution.
- **LangChain remote sandboxes** (Modal/Daytona/Runloop/LocalShell): **deferred, optional** — only if a concrete benchmark needs remote shell/filesystem execution that Monty deliberately forbids.

### Tracing and callbacks

- Existing Tracer, FileCollector, MemoryCollector, and callback event bus preserved.
- Pydantic AI agents emit **legacy-shaped** trace records (`type: agent | llm | tool`) via adapters at the `execute()` boundary, so `BenchmarkReport` needs no changes.

### Dependencies

- POC: add `pydantic-ai-slim[openai]` (covers openai/azure/openrouter/OpenAI-compatible local through one provider).
- Code Mode phase: add `pydantic-ai-harness[code-mode]` (pulls in Monty).
- LangChain `deepagents` / sandbox partner packages: deferred, only if the optional sandbox phase is activated.
- Do not remove existing OpenAI SDK / openai-agents usage until legacy `*_legacy` aliases are deprecated.

### Registration

- New agents and LLM classes register via the existing ComponentABCMeta / AgentManager / ModelManager patterns so YAML `type:` resolution continues to work.

## Testing Decisions

### Principles

- Test **external behavior** at the highest seam possible, not internal Pydantic AI call structure.
- Prefer integration tests over mocking LLM responses when proving migration viability.
- Existing skipped benchmark tests are the template for POC validation; gate live runs behind credential `skipif` rather than a bare `skip`.

### Modules / seams to test

| Seam | Behavior under test | Prior art |
|------|---------------------|-----------|
| BenchmarkRunner + unchanged YAML | Full benchmark run produces evaluation results | `tests/benchmark/mcpuniverse/test_benchmark_*.py` |
| Registry resolution | Legacy `type:` aliases instantiate Pydantic AI-backed classes; `*_legacy` resolves to old ones | `tests/workflow/test_workflow_builder*.py` |
| Provider factory | Each provider produces valid generation | `tests/llm/test_openai.py`, `test_openrouter.py` |
| Executor.execute | Agent returns AgentResponse; invokes MCP tools | `tests/agent/test_function_call.py` |
| Tracing | FileCollector receives `agent/llm/tool` records; `BenchmarkReport.dump()` succeeds | `tests/tracer/test_tracer.py` |
| MCP+ context layer | Large outputs compressed when threshold exceeded | `tests/extensions/mcpplus/integration/test_integration.py` |

### POC test gate

- `financial_analysis` benchmark passes end-to-end with the Pydantic AI function_call agent and `provider: azure`.
- YAML config file unchanged from current version.
- At least one task (`yfinance_task_0001`, the deterministic MSFT date-range task) reports `passed=True`.
- `BenchmarkReport.dump()` generates without trace-shape errors.
- The integration test uses `@pytest.mark.skipif(not os.getenv("AZURE_API_KEY"))` so CI stays green without secrets.

### Out of scope for POC tests

- react and wide research (Phase 1).
- Code Mode / Monty (Code Mode phase).
- MCP+ refactor (its own phase).
- RL rollouts and env_pool docker_pool mode.
- Local LLM providers (their own phase).

## Out of Scope

- Full migration of all agent types in one effort.
- Replacing MCPClient with Pydantic AI / LangChain MCP clients.
- Retiring env_pool in favour of cloud-only sandboxes.
- Replacing MCP+ entirely with Code Mode.
- Adopting the LangChain QuickJS interpreter (redundant with Monty).
- RL / TITO / VERL / react_train_agent migration.
- Custom workflow orchestration migration to LangGraph.
- Benchmark score parity guarantees with legacy agents.
- Removing legacy BaseLLM and BaseAgent in early phases.
- Committing secrets or API keys in tests or configs.

## Further Notes

- **MCP+ vs CE:** "CE" refers to code execution / code-mode (programmatic tool calling), not a named repo component. Code Mode and MCP+ are complementary.
- **Two code-mode engines exist in the ecosystem** — Pydantic AI Code Mode (Monty / Python) and LangChain Deep Agents interpreter (QuickJS / JavaScript). We deliberately choose **only Monty**, since Pydantic AI is the agent runtime and our tools/evaluators are Python.
- **No existing LangChain or Pydantic AI footprint** in the codebase today; the repo ships `pydantic==2.11.7` and `openai-agents==0.2.11` (unrelated to the Pydantic AI agent framework).
- **Design doc** with architecture diagram, phased roadmap, and decision log: [`docs/design/langchain-pydantic-ai-migration.md`](langchain-pydantic-ai-migration.md).
- **Open questions** for follow-up: whether served vllm/sglang endpoints support native tool calling (else react-parse fallback); which remote sandbox provider, if any, is ever needed.
